7048128ad1.q: What is the difference between capital and money in an economy?
7048128ad1.a: Capital is anything you produce—a product or service—while money is what facilitates exchange but has no intrinsic value without capital backing it. Money without capital is meaningless; capital represents real goods and services you create and exchange. When central banks increase money supply by printing currency, that new money has no capital stored in it and must extract capital from existing money already in circulation.

80d0f3b003.q: Why did President Nixon take the United States off the gold standard in 1971?
80d0f3b003.a: President Nixon took the U.S. off the gold standard on August 15, 1971, because countries like France were draining gold from Fort Knox by exchanging U.S. dollars for gold, worried that more dollars were being printed than gold actually existed. The U.S. was under-reserved and spending recklessly, though Nixon had a choice—the choice was to not spend recklessly in the first place.

b1fa16f058.q: How do hedonic adjustments hide true inflation in government statistics?
b1fa16f058.a: Hedonic adjustments artificially lower reported inflation by crediting quality improvements to products even when prices rise. For example, if a Honda Civic's price rises 10 percent but the government claims the car improved 12 percent in quality, they report inflation as minus 2 percent instead of plus 10 percent. From 1996 to 2008, new car prices actually rose about 25 percent, but hedonic adjustments made the government report them as down 15 percent.

9151eb0676.q: What does Paul Musson recommend for individuals to protect themselves from currency devaluation and inflation?
9151eb0676.a: Musson recommends a two-pronged approach: first, invest in hard assets like gold, real estate, and high-quality companies that put capital to productive use, maintaining diversification in things you understand; second, educate yourself and others about how the economy actually works so you can demand better policy decisions from policymakers. He personally holds gold, maintains cash in high-interest savings accounts, and invests in high-quality mutual funds and companies.
